challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: {reliability_ruth} flagged a gap in our current allocation workflow. We are still relying on manual spot checks to verify that the suggested replenishment quantities match the supplier confirmed pallets before the trucks leave the distribution centre. She wants to automate this verification step entirely. The goal is to have a continuous monitoring check that runs without any human intervention, catching discrepancies the moment they appear in the system. This will ensure we catch errors before physical stock is committed, reducing the risk of overstock or stockouts during the promotion week. The team needs this automated guardrail in place immediately to handle the live orders safely.
output.reclassify_reason: The text articulates a strong need for an automated guardrail to handle live orders safely, and implementing it immediately with continuous monitoring would satisfy the stated desire for error-free, human-intervention-free verification.
